Main_Strength: Simple, interpretable coefficients and strong benchmark performance.
Main_Limitation: Residual heteroscedasticity requires robust inference and predictions shrink toward the middle.

Main_Strength: Natural count-model structure with positive fitted means and multiplicative interpretation.
Main_Limitation: Poisson assumes conditional mean and variance are similar; strong overdispersion makes this unsuitable.

Main_Strength: Handles overdispersion better than Poisson while preserving a count-model interpretation.
Main_Limitation: Less straightforward to explain than MLR and still inherits observational-data limitations.

Main_Strength: Stabilizes correlated predictors through coefficient shrinkage.
Main_Limitation: Does not set coefficients exactly to zero and is less directly interpretable after standardization/shrinkage.

Main_Strength: Performs regularization and can remove weak encoded predictors.
Main_Limitation: Selected variables can depend on the tuning period and correlated predictors may be selected unstably.

Main_Strength: Combines Ridge shrinkage and LASSO variable selection.
Main_Limitation: Requires tuning both alpha and lambda and is less transparent to non-technical users.
